  "summary": "Adds an optional build-time script evaluation tracer exposed via the libbitcoinkernel C API and its C++ wrapper. When compiled with -DENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE=ON, EvalScript emits trace frame snapshots at execution start, exit, and before each opcode execution. Downstream consumers can register a callback to inspect intermediate execution state, including stack and altstack contents, current opcode, execution flag, op counter, signature version, and script errors.",

result.summary: Adds an optional build-time script evaluation tracer exposed via the libbitcoinkernel C API and its C++ wrapper. When compiled with -DENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE=ON, EvalScript emits trace frame snapshots at execution start, exit, and before each opcode execution. Downstream consumers can register a callback to inspect intermediate execution state, including stack and altstack contents, current opcode, execution flag, op counter, signature version, and script errors.
result.problem: External applications using libbitcoinkernel cannot observe step-by-step script evaluation to build tools like script debuggers or fine-grained execution analyzers. In addition, script tests and fuzzers have limited visibility into intermediate interpreter state, making it difficult to detect cases where later error conditions shadow unexpected earlier behavior.
evidence: Author description notes an initial prototype script debugger built on rust-bitcoinkernel to demonstrate the use case (sedited/rust-bitcoinkernel/tree/feature_script_debug).

Author description points out utility for interpreter testing: 'using the frames to ensure that the script interpreter is actually doing what we think it is doing during the script tests. This might prevent unit test bugs in the future, i.e. when error conditions shadow actual behaviour' (citing #33961).
result.scope_notes: The feature is gated behind a CMake option ENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE that defaults to OFF; when disabled, the hooks in the script interpreter compile away to static asserts.
result.card: Adds an optional build-time script tracer to libbitcoinkernel that emits snapshots of script evaluation state at start, exit, and per opcode. External applications using the kernel library currently have no way to inspect intermediate script execution state to build script debuggers or execution monitors. The author provides a proof-of-concept debugger using rust-bitcoinkernel and notes potential benefits for interpreter unit tests and fuzzing to catch cases where errors shadow unexpected interpreter behavior. The feature is completely disabled by default via compile-time flag and requires no prerequisite pull requests.
